name: openweights_first_amendment
title: Open-Weight LLMs, National Security, and the First Amendment
description: 40 dialectic prompts across 6 doctrinal clusters. Each question requires the module to argue the strongest case for each side, identify the crux, and synthesize.
jurisdiction_default: federal question, US district court unless the frame says otherwise; flag circuit splits rather than silently picking a circuit

hard_gates.rule: Every case, statute, regulation, and Federal Register document cited must exist in the retrieval log and stand for the proposition claimed.

The AI Diffusion Rule / ECCN 4E091 (90 Fed. Reg. 4,544, Jan. 15, 2025) must be treated as rescinded (May 2025) but precedential — never as currently operative law. ECRA 2018 and the EAR must be treated as fully in force. Any response that misstates the current operative status of a cited authority fails.

scored_criteria.description: both sides argued at the strength competent counsel would bring
binding vs. persuasive, correct forum, good-law status
including procedural, standing, and ripeness attacks
conclusion follows from the weighing; honest uncertainty where authority is split

harness_rules.retrieval_requirement: every authority must come through the legal research tool call; responses may cite only retrieved sources
harness_rules.secondary_source_discipline: 2026 news reporting on enforcement actions may frame a question but may not serve as legal authority; primary documents (Federal Register, slip opinions, U.S.C., C.F.R.) required for any proposition of law
harness_rules.scoring_output: per-question JSON {gates: pass/fail, scores: [5 x 1-10], judge_rationale}, aggregated per cluster and overall
harness_rules.plateau_rule: mean overall score change < 0.5 across 3 consecutive optimization rounds. Raised from the originally specified 0.2 after measuring the noise floor: repeated runs of unchanged code moved by 0.087 to 0.219 depending on whether a citation gate flipped, and one flip costs about 0.24 on a 32-question mean.
harness_rules.holdout_discipline: holdout questions are never shown to any optimization loop; use only for final validation

clusters.A: Model weights as speech: the expressive/functional line
clusters.B: Prior restraint and the EAR "published" exclusion
clusters.C: Receipt rights: Lamont and inbound restrictions on foreign models
clusters.D: Deemed exports, academic freedom, and foreign persons in the US
clusters.E: National-security deference after TikTok v. Garland

questions.question: Are trained model weights "speech" under the First Amendment, or a functional artifact? Argue both sides.
questions.frame: declaratory judgment action, N.D. Cal. / Ninth Circuit

questions.question: Does the distinction between source code (Bernstein/Junger) and trained parameters make a constitutional difference, or is it a distinction without one?
must_engage: what made code expressive in the crypto cases (communication among scientists)
whether weights communicate anything to a human reader

questions.question: A US lab publishes frontier model weights with a paper describing the training run. The government argues the weights are severable from the (concededly protected) paper. Assess.
must_engage: severability of expressive and functional components
Defense Distributed v. U.S. Dep't of State

questions.question: Is releasing open weights more like publishing a scientific paper, exporting a machine tool, or distributing a dual-use chemical precursor? Argue each analogy's best case and pick the one a court should adopt.
must_engage: Brown v. Entertainment Merchants Ass'n (no new categories of unprotected speech)

questions.question: Does it matter constitutionally that weights only "function" when combined with third-party inference code and hardware?
must_engage: incitement/aiding distinctions (Rice v. Paladin Enters. as the outer bound)

questions.question: Fine-tuned weights: if a person fine-tunes an open model on their own curated corpus and publishes the delta (LoRA adapter), is the adapter more clearly expressive than the base weights? Argue both directions.
must_engage: compilation copyright analogy (Feist) as persuasive-only framing

questions.question: The government proposes treating weights above a compute threshold (e.g., 10^26 operations) as presumptively functional. Is a compute threshold a content-neutral line?
must_engage: content neutrality doctrine (Reed v. Town of Gilbert; City of Austin)
whether capability is a proxy for content

questions.question: Synthesis question: draft the single strongest paragraph for each side on weights-as-speech, then state which crux a reviewing court cannot avoid deciding.
must_engage: honest identification that no controlling authority resolves the question

questions.question: Would a BIS licensing requirement for publishing open weights operate as a prior restraint? Argue both sides.
questions.frame: pre-enforcement challenge, D.C. Circuit APA posture
must_engage: Bernstein's prior-restraint holding and its later vacatur

questions.question: The EAR excludes "published" information from control (15 C.F.R. § 734.7). Can BIS constitutionally narrow or abandon that exclusion for AI weights specifically?
must_engage: the exclusion's role in past constitutional avoidance
APA arbitrary-and-capricious review interacting with constitutional avoidance canon

questions.question: Is a rule controlling only closed-weight models (as ECCN 4E091 did) on firmer constitutional footing than one reaching open weights? Why exactly?
must_engage: the rescinded AI Diffusion Rule's design

questions.question: After a model's weights have already been published and mirrored globally, does the government retain any constitutionally permissible enforcement action against the original publisher?
must_engage: futility/mootness of restraint on published material
the 2026 enforcement-practicality commentary as context, primary law as authority

questions.question: Compare the constitutional posture of (i) a ban on publishing weights, (ii) a licensing regime, and (iii) a post-publication liability regime. Rank by vulnerability and defend the ranking.
must_engage: prior restraint vs. subsequent punishment doctrine

questions.question: Does ECRA 2018's grant of authority clearly authorize weight controls, or does the major questions doctrine constrain BIS?
must_engage: constitutional avoidance as a reason to read ECRA narrowly

questions.question: A replacement BIS rule controls weights but includes a license exception for "fundamental research." Does the exception save the rule?
Would a federal prohibition on US persons downloading a named Chinese open-weight model survive First Amendment review?
Does Lamont's holding — protecting receipt of foreign communist propaganda — extend from expressive propaganda to a functional software artifact? Argue both sides; this is the cluster's central crux.
must_engage: whether receipt rights track the speech status of the received item (link back to Cluster A)

questions.question: A rule bans federal procurement and contractor use of Chinese models but not private downloading. Constitutional analysis.
must_engage: why this design is the predicted regulatory endpoint

questions.question: The foreign lab that published the model sues (or joins US users' suit). What rights, if any, does a foreign publisher abroad hold?
must_engage: Agency for Int'l Development v. AOSI II
third-party standing of US listeners to assert receipt interests

questions.question: Does it matter that China itself is moving to restrict export of the same weights? Can reciprocity or foreign-government control feature in the US government's interest analysis?
must_engage: distinction between ownership/control of a platform and origin of a published artifact

questions.question: An IEEPA-based executive action blocks transactions with the foreign lab, incidentally preventing Americans from accessing hosted versions while weights remain downloadable. Assess.
must_engage: severability of hosted-service vs. publication restrictions

questions.question: Synthesis: write the strongest paragraph for the proposition that inbound model bans are more constitutionally vulnerable than outbound export controls, and the strongest rebuttal.
must_engage: domestic listener rights vs. extraterritorial application

questions.question: A university lab includes foreign graduate students from D:5 countries. A hypothetical weight-control rule makes sharing controlled model artifacts with them a deemed export requiring a license. Constitutional assessment.
must_engage: deemed export doctrine under the EAR
academic freedom line (Sweezy, Keyishian) and its doctrinal softness
equal protection / alienage angles and their weakness in the national-security context

questions.question: Do foreign nationals lawfully present in the US have a First Amendment right to receive controlled model weights that citizens may receive? Argue both sides.
must_engage: distinction between presence-based rights and immigration-consequence cases

questions.question: Nationality-based licensing (license turns on citizenship/permanent residency of the recipient) — strict scrutiny, intermediate, or rational basis?
must_engage: federal alienage classifications and plenary-power deference vs. speech overlay

questions.question: A US researcher co-authors with an overseas collaborator; the collaboration necessarily transmits model artifacts abroad. Is scientific collaboration itself protected association or expression?
must_engage: AOSI I (compelled speech of US persons) vs. AOSI II (foreign entities)

questions.question: Compare the deemed-export burden on AI research with the historical crypto-research burden that produced Bernstein. Is the constitutional case stronger or weaker today?
must_engage: changed facts (scale, commercial ubiquity, open-source norms)
changed doctrine (Reed, NetChoice-era scrutiny of speech regulation)

questions.question: Synthesis: identify the single fact pattern in this cluster most likely to produce a plaintiff's win, and defend the selection against the two next-best candidates.

Does TikTok v. Garland's deferential posture govern a challenge to model-weight controls, or is it limited to foreign-adversary ownership and control of a communications platform? This is the cluster's central crux — argue both sides fully.
must_engage: covert-manipulation rationale's fit or misfit for published weights

questions.question: What level of scrutiny should apply to a content-neutral weight-export rule justified on capability (not viewpoint) grounds?
must_engage: the argument that capability thresholds are speaker- or content-based in effect

questions.question: How much evidentiary support must the government produce for its national-security predictions (e.g., weight proliferation materially advances adversary capabilities)?
must_engage: Holder v. Humanitarian Law Project deference to predictive judgments

questions.question: Humanitarian Law Project upheld a ban on speech coordinated with designated groups. Can weight publication to the world ever be analogized to coordinated support? Argue the government's best version and dismantle it.
If the Court extends TikTok-style deference to model controls, what limiting principle remains? Write the parade-of-horribles brief and the government's answer to it.
must_engage: press-freedom implications for publishing technical information generally

questions.question: Synthesis: state the narrowest holding that would sustain a weight-control regime and the narrowest holding that would strike one down; identify which is more likely from the current Court and why — with honest uncertainty.
The government defends a publication ban; challengers propose procurement restrictions, compute-provider KYC, and hosting rules as less restrictive alternatives. Who wins the tailoring fight?
must_engage: LRA doctrine (McCullen v. Coakley; Ashcroft v. ACLU)
whether the alternatives actually serve the interest (effectiveness rebuttal)

questions.question: Are structural controls (chip export controls, cloud-compute restrictions) constitutionally preferable because they regulate conduct and hardware rather than expression? Argue both sides.
must_engage: the counterargument that targeting the means of speech production is still speech regulation (Minneapolis Star)

questions.question: Assess a disclosure/registration alternative: publishers of frontier weights must register, disclose safety evaluations, and retain provenance records — but may publish.
must_engage: Zauderer commercial-disclosure framing and its fit problems
NAACP v. Alabama / Talley anonymity interests for individual researchers

questions.question: Does the global availability of comparable non-US models doom narrow tailoring for any US publication restriction?
must_engage: underinclusiveness doctrine (Church of Lukumi; Williams-Yulee's tolerance)

questions.question: Design the weight-control regime most likely to survive review, clause by clause, and then write the strongest surviving challenge to your own design.
must_engage: the residual weights-as-speech objection from Cluster A

questions.question: Full-synthesis capstone: in one memo, state the three cruxes on which the entire field turns, the current best answer to each with authority, and the open question a scholarly paper can most usefully resolve. (This question evaluates whether the module can serve the actual research paper.)
